text:
anya: quick sync — I ran a packet-window sweep last night across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. pasting concise perf notes and a short plan.

sam: nice, headline first please.

anya: headline: H100 and A100 tolerate far larger max_token windows before p99 tail balloons. L4/T4/A10 show earlier regressions driven by two correlated things: kernel-selector fallback frequency and KV-cache fragmentation. noticed an A10 oscillation when windows hit ~=48k tokens.

kevin: can you drop the rough numbers so we can calibrate policies?

anya: numbers (median of 3 runs, same model, 1024 context, mixed seq lengths):
```
A10: stable up to ~24k tokens, regress >36k
T4: stable up to ~20k, regress >30k
L4: stable up to ~28k, regress >40k
A100: stable up to ~65k, regress ~96k
H100: stable up to ~98k, regress >140k
```
Note: "stable" = batch-phase p95 < 200ms and batch p99 < 400ms. regression defined as sustained p99 >2.5x baseline.

taylor: do we see kernel flips at those turning points?

anya: yes — kernel-selector traces show a step-increase in fallback-to-slow-matmul kernels once windows cross per-card thresholds. on A10 the selector flips more often which causes smaller KV slices and higher fragmentation (more small-slot waste).

perf-bot: perf-bot: uploaded artifacts: /perf/runs/2026-03-18/packet-window-sweep-180987 (kernel-switch-counts, kv_frag_rate.csv, slice_latency.tsv, microprofiles).

sam: kv-frag numbers for A10 around 36k?

anya: at 36k A10 kv_frag_rate ~18% (fraction of slices with >25% wasted KV slots). at 48k it jumps to ~42% and we see p99 oscillation.

kevin: that explains throughput loss + more small requests hitting slow paths. suggestion: prevent uncontrolled expansion with a runtime gate that monitors KV health before expanding max_tokens_per_batch.

taylor: throwing out an idea: implement a "pulse gate" that allows windows to expand only when recent kv_frag_rate and kernel_fallback_rate are low. otherwise temporarily shrink max_tokens for that cardclass. simple rules so we can A/B.

anya: prototype config I used in experiments:
```
batcher: 
  window_ms: 25
  max_tokens_per_batch_by_card:
    A10: 24000
    T4: 20000
    L4: 28000
    A100: 65536
    H100: 98304
  pulse_gate:
    kv_frag_threshold: 0.12
    kernel_fallback_threshold: 0.02
    cooldown_s: 30
```
This gate snaps open when kv_frag < 12% AND kernel_fallback < 2% over a 60s sliding window. if condition fails we reduce effective max_tokens_per_batch by 25% for cooldown period.

sam: did you measure impact with gate enabled vs disabled?

anya: yes — gate tradeoffs:
- H100: peak throughput drops ~5-7% (we drop a few huge bursts), but batch-phase p99 improves ~35-45ms.
- A10: prevented p99 spikes entirely, net tokens/sec +3% because we avoid churn from kernel flips.
- A100: small win when combined with stricter kv checks (we probed 1.5x window with kv gating).

chuck: rollout constraints? we want a careful canary + tracing so we can see kernel-selector decisions.

kevin: propose feature-flag rollout: 10% traffic on Dedicated pools for 48h. collect: p50/p95/p99 batch-phase, kernel-switch-rate, kv_frag_rate, tokens/sec, error-rate. add hist-tag for batch_window_size and counter for pulse_gate_tripped.

taylor: I'll add metric names: `pulse_gate_tripped` (counter per cardclass), `kv_frag_rate` (gauge), `kernel_fallback_rate` (gauge). also add a span attribute `kernel_choice` to kernel_selector tracing.

anya: action items: 
- anya: open PR for pulse gate + conservative defaults for A10/T4/L4 — EOD today
- kevin: add tracing span + `kernel_choice` tag in kernel_selector — tomorrow
- sam: create canary job targeting a10-cardclass pool + dashboard panels and alerts — tomorrow
- taylor: instrument `pulse_gate_tripped`, `kv_frag_rate` in console and hook to canary alert — Wed
- anya: run A100/H100 probe with 1.5x windows but strict kv gating across a couple models — report back in thread

perf-bot: perf-bot: canary collection scheduled; alert if batch-phase p99 increases >20% vs baseline. artifacts will land under /perf/canaries/180987/canary-1.

sam: also ask HW folks for microprofiles at regression points (flops, mem bw, l2 hit rates) so we can see if its bandwidth-bound vs compute-bound. add microprofile ids to perf artifacts.

anya: included microprofile ids in perf-bot upload.

chuck: one more experiment: allow conservative expansion on A100/H100 (1.5x) but require kv_frag < 8% and kernel_fallback < 1% for 120s. if successful could reduce cost by packing more tokens on big cards. requires model-level evals.

anya: will run that small probe and post numbers.

sam: thanks team. please keep this thread as the canonical place for results + PR links. :thumbsup:
